A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EventVGGT and support comparison of the text, equations, seven figures, and eight tables. All 12 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original EventVGGT evaluations on EventScape, MVSEC, and DENSE, component and sensitivity ablations, and qualitative geometric reconstructions.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative depth, camera-pose, and point-cloud results.

M1.justification: The stated losses receive limited revisions: Eq. (1) switches from mixed-output confidence to RGB-teacher confidence, and Eq. (3) uses mixed depths instead of event-only depths. The architecture, three modules, and loss weights remain unchanged. An implementation change is not established: v1's Fig. 2 already connects TCD to mixed depths.

E1.justification: Both versions use EventScape, MVSEC, and DENSE for the same depth-estimation and zero-shot evaluations, including the same day/night scenarios. The camera-pose and point-cloud demonstrations are also retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds EReFormer to the MVSEC comparison in Table 2. All previous comparators in Tables 1–4 remain; the other newly cited work is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, 10/20/30m depth-error and delta metrics, 24-frame inputs, and training settings are unchanged. EReFormer is added within the existing MVSEC comparison without a reported protocol revision.

E4.justification: Tables 5–8 retain the same component, sequence-length, mixture-rate, and training-diversity ablations. The far-field error example and qualitative reconstruction/consistency analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The confidence-weighted training loss is a method component, not uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds 12 EReFormer error entries, including 30m errors of 2.98, 2.66, 2.68, and 2.59 for Night1, Night2, Night3, and Day1. All pre-existing numerical results and qualitative examples are retained; no EventVGGT performance improvement between versions is reported.

T1.justification: Eqs. (1) and (3) revise the formal loss definitions through the confidence-source and depth-variable substitutions. These are not equivalent notation changes. Eqs. (2) and (4) remain equivalent, and no new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, tri-level distillation, temporal consistency, benchmark superiority, zero-shot transfer, and auxiliary 3D-task claims. The highlighted EventScape reduction from 2.30 to 1.06 is unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of temporal robustness, mixture-rate behavior, training diversity, and inherited far-field depth compression. The limitation and proposed future use of ground-truth depth for calibration are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link to the abstract; v1 provides no corresponding access information. Implementation settings, hardware, training time, and inference timing remain unchanged. Repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to High-rate monocular depth estimation via cross frame-rate collaboration of frames and events, and Event-based monocular depth estimation with recurrent transformers. The latter supports the EReFormer comparison. Existing research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. v2 adds keywords and acknowledgments, updates affiliation and author-role notes, makes small wording edits, and repairs the unresolved Table reference in Section 3.3 to Table 7.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column formatting, with substantially different margins, typography, figure/table sizes, placements, captions, and table rules. Figures 3 and 4 exchange numbering and positions, Fig. 2 gains a Mixture legend entry, and Table 2 gains the EReFormer row.

improvement.justification: The EReFormer comparison, code link, and repaired Table 7 reference provide limited benefits, and Eq. (3) now agrees with the mixed-depth path already shown in Fig. 2. However, Eq. (1) now specifies teacher confidence while its accompanying prose still specifies mixed-output confidence. The unexplained loss revisions and unchanged results leave the implemented objective unresolved, so these benefits and harms do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
